email.subject: Where does the expense policy live
email.preview_text: The question that keeps landing in your Slack. A no-code agent over the handbook answers it instead of you.
email.headline: The Slack answer-bot is now a configuration
email.body:
Someone asks in Slack where the expense policy lives. The answer is in the handbook, four pages deep, and asking you is faster than finding it.

The fix is easy to scope and hard to start. A bot in the channel over the handbook — then a vector store and a Slack event pipeline that somebody keeps running afterwards, on a team where nobody owns internal tooling.

orqAgent is a no-code platform for building AI agents, and that part is now configuration. You upload the policy documents; the agent retrieves the relevant context for every query, with **no vector DB to manage**.

Slack is a native channel, installed by OAuth — the bot replies to mentions and channel messages. The platform is serverless and scales automatically, so there is no infrastructure left over for you to own once it works.

Create one agent, give it one policy document, and ask it a question in the channel. The plumbing is settled; whether it answers well on your own handbook is the part worth testing. **Free to start, no card required.**
email.call_to_action: Point it at one policy document
email.postscript: Setup runs from the console — the first agent takes under two minutes.

email.subject: Handbook answers in Slack, without the build
email.preview_text: Upload one policy document, connect Slack by OAuth install, and judge the answers yourself.
email.body:
If a Slack bot over the company handbook has been on your list for a while, this is the part that changed.

orqAgent is a no-code platform for building AI agents. You upload PDFs, docs or plain text, and the agent retrieves the relevant context for every query — **no vector DB to manage**.

Slack is a native channel, connected by OAuth install; the bot replies to mentions and channel messages. So the two pieces that usually turn this into a project — the retrieval layer and the event plumbing — are configuration in a console.

Which answers the question worth asking before you start anything: what is left for you to keep running. No vector store, no event pipeline, nothing of yours sitting in a server somewhere — the platform is serverless, zero infrastructure to manage.

What that cannot tell you is whether the answers are good on your documents. Create one agent, give it the policy document you get asked about most, and ask it a question in the channel. Free to start, no card required.
email.postscript: Setup runs from the console — the first agent takes under two minutes.
